key_insight: ScholarCatalyst introduces a benchmark for measuring whether AI systems can retrieve earlier papers that actually inspired later research, not just broadly relevant papers. The key idea is to test a higher-level scholarly skill: finding the prior work that sparks new ideas.
problem_solved: Current retrieval systems are good at finding related literature, but they do not capture which papers truly helped researchers generate or complete a new project. This paper addresses the lack of a benchmark for identifying inspirational, idea-advancing papers in large research archives.
method: Builds a benchmark from researchers’ own annotations of which prior papers influenced their completed projects.
Uses an automated pipeline to scale author annotation across many papers and projects.
Frames retrieval as a task of finding papers that inspired new research, rather than only those that are topically similar.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark offers a more realistic test of research-assistant systems and scholarly search tools. It can guide the development of tools that help scientists discover foundational ideas, not just matching keywords.

paper_title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
paper_authors: Sohyeon Kim, Yoonho Lee, Bo Liu, Dayoon Ko, Rulin Shao
